verdict.rationale: 2FAS explicitly markets its code as inspectable ('take a look at our code', GitHub repos for both auth and pass browser extensions) and states 'Source-available code ensures that every security feature we use can be verified by independent security experts,' directly matching the story's claim of community-reviewable seed-handling code. The probe confirms llms.txt describes 2FAS Auth as 'open-source.' Missing for 10: independent third-party audit reports or concrete evidence of community-submitted security reviews/PRs, and clarity on whether 'source-available' vs fully OSI-licensed open source applies uniformly across all client apps.
